claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi and is never sent to the cloud provider.
A GCP Cloud SQL instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is a cloud-provider deletion-protection setting.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to provider-side deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider-side deletion protection is off.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, that the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.
GCP Cloud SQL instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (as exposed in Pulumi's GCP provider) that enforces deletion protection independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
AWS RDS instances have a `deletionProtection` attribute (as exposed in Pulumi's AWS provider) that enforces deletion protection independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and provider/cloud-level deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page on destroy-failures troubleshooting has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) that explains how to tell apart Pulumi `protect` and resource-level deletion protection and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Three distinct layers can hold deletion protection that causes a `pulumi destroy` failure: Pulumi's protect option, a provider-enforced flag, and a cloud-API-enforced protection.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider, and the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` property.

AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are enforced by the cloud API, which rejects the delete call independent of Pulumi; the error can carry a code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough.
To remove deletion protection: set the attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` `deletionProtection` is provider-enforced.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is true.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` `deletionProtection` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` `forceDestroy` defaults to false, and a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` `disableApiTermination` is enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` `deletionProtectionEnabled` is enforced by the AWS API and defaults to false.

`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; a `CanNotDelete` lock enforced by Azure Resource Manager must be removed before the resource can be deleted.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
The docs page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the protect option.
